newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil eases on futures, premiums firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil eases on futures, premiums firm.

text.p: NWE gas oil ended steady to slightly lower on Friday as benchmark IPE futures eased, but traders said the physical market remained firm and premiums were strong. The September IPE contract settled unchanged at $196.75 a tonne. The October contract ended 25 cents lower at $193.75. Low sulphur cargo premiums were talked at Oct IPE +$13, cif NWE. Traders said a number of players were hanging on to cargoes on the expectation that premiums will strengthen further ahead of the introduction of low sulphur regulations on October 1.

The German heating oil market was also seen strengthening. Premiums continued to be talked at Sept IPE +4.50/5.0 for September 10-20. Traders said suppliers were gearing up for an upturn in German end-user demand as autumn draws nearer.
They also noted that a GOM cargo was done at Sept IPE +$6.50, cif Le havre so it was not surprising to see German heating oil premiums also climbing higher.
On the heating oil barges, traders said premiums were stuck around the Oct IPE +50 cents/$2.0 level. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7714.
